Subject: Pathway metering: unify cost + latency by execution path

Team —

ACME raised an ask today that I think points to a broader gap in our Console: they want to see cost and tail-latency not only by endpoint/route, but broken down by "execution path" (e.g., prompt template → external tool call → long context decode) so they can identify which parts of a flow are driving token spend vs tail latency.

Proposal: a small POC that emits a "pathway id" tag for each request (derived from route + template id + tool-call-signature), and a Console tile that shows: aggregated token-cost, p95/p99 latency, and sample traces per pathway.

Asks:
- Marcus: feasibility / POC timeline (ops or infra work?)
- Olga: telemetry footprint and storage implications (sampling, approximate cardinality expectations)
- Lauren: dashboard UX and retention implications (what prism of time + filters make this useful?)
- Camila: will Sales/CS find this valuable for renewals + escalation root cause?

I've attached a short write-up and a couple of example SQL queries that ACME shared. If this lands well we can surface it as an "execution path" view in the Route Explorer.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pathway-metrics-proposal.pdf (7 pages), example-query-samples.sql

Avery —

I like the framing. From a product/roadmap angle I'd treat this as two deliverables:
1) POC telemetry pipeline + sampling strategy (3w) — proves we can tag and persist pathway aggregates without exploding storage.
2) Console surfaces (tile + drilldown + sample trace playback) (4–6w) once we agree on the aggregation schema.

We should scope the POC tightly: limit to 10 heavy customers (ACME included), one region, and a single model family to control cardinality. If Ops agrees to a sampling budget, we can avoid a large infra lift.

I'll add this to the roadmap candidate list and propose we demo in the next weekly product review.

Quick technical notes from infra:

- Tagging: adding a pathway_id to the request envelope is cheap (metadata only). The hard part is cardinality — if customers generate N templates * M tool variants * K models, pathway combos blow up quickly.
- Sampling: we recommend a two-tier approach: always capture full metadata + samples for the top 50 pathways by request volume per tenant, and reservoir-sample the rest at 1–5% depending on tenant tier.
- Storage: storing per-pathway aggregates (counts, sum_tokens, sum_cost, p95/p99 approximations using HDR histograms) is feasible in our TS store. Raw traces should be sampled to object store. Expect additional monthly cost; rough estimate for 10 customers in POC: +$2k/month for metrics retention and +$0.6k for sampled traces.
- Queryability: export the pathway index to BigQuery (or internal analytics cluster) nightly for ad-hoc slicing. Attached a small example of the SQL we used to prototype p95 by pathway.

If product signs off on the sampling knobs and retention tiering, infra can spin up the ingestion within 2–3 weeks for a scoped POC.

— Olga
Infrastructure Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few UX/ops considerations from Observability: 

- Retention tiers: we should expose pathway-level retention per customer (30/90/365) and signal the cost impact in the Console when toggled.
- Filters: default view = top 20 pathways last 7d, with quick pivot to p95 tail latency. Allow drilldown to example traces + raw request payload (redacted).
- Alerts: we can surface pathway-level anomaly alerts (sudden cost spikes or tail latency regressions). Need product to confirm default thresholds or whether customers will provide example-scenarios.

I can prototype the Console tile in Figma this week and will push a short spec to the doc link. If everyone is ok, we should open a JIRA (RED-9432) and schedule a cross-functional sync next Tuesday.

-Lauren
